summary.text: A 25-year-old primigravid woman with an unremarkable medical and obstetric history was referred to a fetal medicine clinic for a fetal intraabdominal cystic mass seen on routine ultrasound. At 39 weeks of gestation advanced ultrasound showed an 80 × 60 × 40 mm retrovesical oval midline pelvic cystic mass with internal echoes; minimal calyceal dilation of both kidneys was also reported.

The fetal bladder had normal outline and volume, other systems showed no abnormality, the amniotic fluid volume was normal and the biophysical profile was reassuring. After counseling, labor was induced with oxytocin and a 3200-g female alive newborn was delivered vaginally.

Immediately after delivery the newborn had a bulging imperforate hymen and a distended abdomen with normal perineum, anus and urethral orifice. Neonatal ultrasound showed a 100 × 70 × 40 mm oval cystic pelvic mass and mild bilateral calyceal dilation, and renal function was normal. Hymenectomy on the second day removed around 200 mL of milky fluid.

The distention was relieved and the calyceal dilation disappeared. Ultrasound after the procedure showed an empty uterus and vagina and the newborn was discharged improved. At a checkup after 2 weeks she was doing well with normal hymen remnants and vaginal orifice.
